description: Worked delta-plan record (AES-V2.18 / SUE-610) for the 'Professional Report -> age 10-12' case worked through in docs/architecture/SOURCE-TARGET-DELTA-PLANNING.md §6. Used by scripts/test-delta.mjs. Not a real editorial judgement.

source_profile.language_quality: The draft is fluent, correctly spaced, and free of translationese in the sampled paragraphs; it reads as professionally edited Korean prose.
source_profile.genre: Written in the Report register: dense evidentiary cadence, numbered findings, hedged claims with confidence qualifiers.
source_profile.audience: Addressed to a domain-practitioner: acronyms unglossed, prerequisite knowledge assumed, no scaffolding for a first-time reader of the topic.
source_profile.knowledge_depth: Carries mechanism (why the effect occurs) and quantified evidence (three cited measurements) beyond a surface-level claim.
source_profile.register: Formal, third-person, evidence-first paragraph structure typical of a practitioner-facing Report.
source_profile.information_structure: Findings-first hierarchy: conclusion stated, then evidence, then caveats, matching a Report's expected shape for its actual audience.
source_profile.terminology: Uses the field's technical terms in their standard professional form (e.g. the untranslated English acronym), consistent with what a practitioner reaches for.

target_profile.language_quality: No language-quality gap implied by the audience change; the target still needs correct, fluent, native Korean.
target_profile.genre: Still a Research piece, but the child-appropriate treatment of a Research piece foregrounds narrative framing over dense evidentiary cadence.
target_profile.audience: A ten-year-old reader with no prerequisite knowledge: every technical term must be glossed or replaced, sentences short, one idea per sentence.
target_profile.knowledge_depth: Mechanism must be simplified to a single causal chain a ten-year-old can follow; the three quantified measurements are not requested at this depth.
target_profile.register: Warm, concrete, second-person-adjacent narration rather than a formal third-person evidentiary register.
target_profile.information_structure: Curiosity-first ordering (what happened, then why) rather than findings-first, matching how the audience profile expects material to be sequenced for this age.
target_profile.terminology: Every technical term needs a plain-language surface form; the untranslated acronym a practitioner reaches for means nothing to this reader.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The sampled paragraphs show no misspelling, spacing error, or translationese scaffolding.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: The target requires correct, fluent Korean, which the source already is.
axis_deltas.evidence: Paragraphs 1-3 of the source draft, checked against the ko-KR pack's normative and native-fluency rules, show zero defects.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The piece is written in the Report register: numbered findings, hedged claims, evidence-first paragraphs.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: A Research piece for a child reader still needs to argue a thesis, but the practitioner Report's dense evidentiary cadence is not the register a ten-year-old's Research piece uses.
axis_deltas.evidence: Section 2 opens with 'Finding 1 (p<0.05):', a Report-register construction absent from every child-audience Research piece in the corpus.

axis_deltas.source_observation: Acronyms are unglossed, prerequisite domain knowledge is assumed throughout, and no sentence offers a first-time reader a foothold.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: A ten-year-old reader needs every term glossed, no assumed prerequisite knowledge, and short single-idea sentences.
axis_deltas.evidence: The opening sentence uses three unglossed acronyms and one subordinate clause with two embedded qualifiers.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The draft carries three quantified measurements and a multi-step causal mechanism explaining the effect.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: The target audience profile calls for a single causal chain a ten-year-old can hold in mind, with the quantified measurements omitted.
axis_deltas.evidence: Paragraph 4 chains four causal steps in one sentence, each with its own numeric qualifier.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The draft is formal and third-person throughout, with no direct address to the reader.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: The audience profile calls for warm, concrete narration, closer to second person, rather than formal third-person exposition.
axis_deltas.evidence: Every paragraph in the sample uses third-person passive constructions with no direct reader address.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The draft states the conclusion first, then evidence, then caveats — a findings-first hierarchy.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: The audience profile calls for curiosity-first ordering: what happened, then why, before any caveat.
axis_deltas.evidence: The first paragraph states the conclusion in its first sentence, before any narrative context is given.

axis_deltas.source_observation: The draft retains the field's English acronym in its standard professional form, per the language pack's keep_source rendering_policy for practitioners.
axis_deltas.target_requirement: The audience profile requires a plain-language surface form for every technical term; the untranslated acronym communicates nothing to this reader.
axis_deltas.evidence: The acronym appears six times in the sample with no gloss or plain-language alias offered anywhere in the draft.

plan_intervention.rationale: audience, knowledge_depth, and terminology all measure LARGE — the highest single-axis intervention is the ceiling; it is not computed by summing or averaging the seven axes.
